question: For the patients whose total cholesterol is higher than normal, how many of them have a negative measure of degree of coagulation?
evidence: total cholesterol is higher than normal refers to `T-CHO` > = 250; negative measure of degree of coagulation refers to KCT = '-' ;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2."T-CHO" >= 250 AND T3.KCT = '-'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND T3.KCT = '-'

b.request: How many distinct patients (counting each ID once) have at least one Laboratory record with `T-CHO` >= 250 and at least one Examination record with KCT = '-'?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID = P.ID AND L.`T-CHO` >= 250) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination E WHERE E.ID = P.ID AND E.KCT = '-')

d.request: For the patients whose total cholesterol is higher than normal (`T-CHO` >= 250), how many of them have a negative measure of degree of coagulation (KCT = '-')? Count each distinct ID only once.
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) FROM Examination AS E INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON E.ID = L.ID WHERE L.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND E.KCT = '-'
